papers.title: Lomb--Scargle Spectroscopy of Non-Polar Interface Traps Governing Anomalous PBTI in GaN FinFETs
papers.summary: In this letter, a spectroscopic framework based on the Lomb-Scargle periodogram is proposed to resolve multi-interface trapping dynamics in GaN FinFETs under positive bias temperature instability (PBTI) stress. Unlike conventional Fourier analysis and discrete multi-exponential fitting, this approach exploits an orthogonal sinusoidal basis for non-uniformly sampled V TH transients, providing a relaxation-frequency representation from which the relaxation-time distribution can be inferred through frequency-to-timescale mapping and physical validation without predefined trapping components. Combined with a facet-de-embedding strategy, the framework isolates the non-polar sidewall-related contribution, whose subsequent Arrhenius analysis reveals a broadened trap-energy distribution centered at 0.54 eV, corroborated by independent DLTS measurements. Furthermore, the extracted power spectrum serves as a weighting function in a dual-channel convolution model, quantitatively reproducing the anomalous temperature-dependent $\Delta $ V TH crossover via the redistribution of trapping contributions across different characteristic time constants. This frequency-domain framework provides a complementary tool for trap-dynamics analysis in multi-gate GaN devices.

papers.title: Preserved p-type performance of MoTe2 transistors via TeO2 dielectric buffer
papers.summary: Two-dimensional (2D) semiconductors show great promise for the post-Moore era, but the high-quality dielectric deposition remains a critical challenge. This is especially true for p-type 2D field-effect transistors (FETs), where precursor-induced n-type doping on the 2D channel severely changes their pristine properties. Here, we propose a TeO2 buffer layer strategy to alleviate this doping issue. The dielectric buffer protects the 2D channel (MoTe2) from interaction with precursors during dielectric deposition, and provides nucleation sites to facilitate uniform and dense dielectric growth. The TeO2/HfO2 hybrid dielectric layers show good uniformity and a high dielectric constant of 18.6. With the TeO2 buffer, the devices achieve a p-type on/off ratio of ∼106 and a small threshold voltage shift. In addition, this strategy is applicable to various contact metals and enables the fabrication of top-gate p-type FETs. This approach offers a viable pathway for integrating p-type 2D FETs and advances the realization of 2D material-based CMOS technology.

papers.title: Switching Losses and Their Mitigation in Lateral β -Ga 2 O 3 Power MOSFETs With High-Permittivity Dielectric for Field Management
papers.summary: Ultrawide-bandgap beta-phase gallium oxide ( $\beta $ -Ga 2 O ${}_{{3}}\text {)}$ is promising for high-voltage, low-loss power devices. Field management in $\beta $ -Ga 2 O 3 transistors using a high-permittivity (high- ${k}\text {)}$ dielectric can improve the devices’ power figure of merit (PFOM), but the increased drain-to-gate feedback capacitance degrades switching performance. This article reports on a simulation study of the switching losses and their mitigation in a 3.3-kV normally- off lateral $\beta $ -Ga 2 O 3 MOSFET with high- $k$ field management. A source-connected field plate (sFP) is proposed to mitigate the switching losses while maintaining the device’s blocking capability. Under the switching condition of 3.3 kV/20 A, the fall time and rise time are reduced by approximately 61% and 85%, respectively. The associated turn-off and turn-on losses decrease by approximately 63% and 51%, respectively. Meanwhile, the sFP can shield the gate from a high drain bias and improve gate stability. The effect of the sFP in mitigating switching losses is more effective at higher load currents, indicating that the proposed strategy is suitable for high-load switching scenarios. These findings provide guiding principles for the design of lateral $\beta $ -Ga 2 O 3 MOSFETs to meet switching requirements in power electronics.

papers.title: Impact of Interface and Dielectric Defects on HKMG MOSFETs Down to Cryogenic Temperatures
papers.summary: This study investigates the impact of interface and dielectric defects on high- $\boldsymbol {\kappa }$ metal gate (HKMG) MOSFETs at cryogenic temperatures, focusing on key MOSFET metrics and their correlation with room temperature values. We use substrate injectors to induce a controlled generation of interface and dielectric defects on devices with a scaled CMOS gate dielectric stack with SiO 2 interlayer, HfO 2 , and gate metal. We evaluate how these defects affect subthreshold swing (SS), threshold voltage, gate leakage, transconductance, and 1/f noise down to cryogenic temperatures by comparing fresh devices and devices subjected to controlled substrate hot-carrier stress prior to cryogenic characterization. The findings are then validated on devices fabricated in commercial FDSOI MOSFETs, using test structures designed to induce varying plasma damage and dielectric defectivity, confirming the robustness of the observed trends across technologies.

papers.title: Synergistic Coupling Effects of Out-of-Plane and In-Plane Polarization in α -In 2 Se 3 Ferroelectric Semiconductor Field-Effect Transistor
papers.summary: The coupling effects of out-of-plane (OOP) and in-plane (IP) polarization in two-dimensional $\alpha $ -In 2 Se 3 based ferroelectric semiconductor-field effect transistor (FeS-FET) are revealed based on TCAD simulation. It is found that single-directional OOP or IP polarization cannot effectively modulate the device state. In contrast, the coupled OOP and IP polarizations significantly regulate the electric field and carrier distribution within FeS channel, endowing a large memory window and a high on/off ratio, which can be attributed to the synergistic enhancement effect of coupled OOP/IP polarization. These results give new insights into operation mechanism and optimization design of FeS-FET as novel ferroelectric memory.

papers.title: 1.6-GW/cm <sup>2</sup> Baliga’s Figure-of-Merit Au-Free p-GaN Gate HEMTs on 6-in Si Enabled by Regrown Ohmic Contacts
papers.summary: High-performance p-GaN/AlGaN/GaN high electron mobility transistors (HEMTs) on 6-inch Si were demonstrated using a CMOS-compatible, Au-free ohmic scheme. Selective MOCVD regrowth of heavily Si-doped n + -InGaN yielded an excellent low wafer-level average contact resistance (R ${}_{\text {c}}\text {)}$ of $0.14~\Omega \cdot $ mm. The integration of regrown ohmic contacts with a dual field-plate architecture, comprising lateral and vertical components, effectively redistributed the electric field and enhanced breakdown performance. For devices with a $15~\mu $ m gate–drain spacing, a threshold voltage of 1 V, a saturation drain current of 465 mA/mm, and an on-resistance (R ${}_{\text {on}}\text {)}$ of $7.2~\Omega \cdot $ mm were achieved, along with an off-state breakdown voltage of 1620 V. These metrics correspond to a Baliga’s figure of merit of 1.6 GW/cm 2 , indicating competitive performance among GaN-on-Si p-GaN HEMTs. Across the 6-inch wafer, both contact resistance and channel sheet resistance exhibited tight distributions, underscoring the manufacturability and process uniformity of the Au-free approach within Si CMOS production lines. This scalable, contamination-free process provides a practical pathway toward high-volume production of GaN power devices with robust electrical performance and CMOS fab compatibility.

papers.title: Wafer-Scale Demonstration of High-Voltage β -Ga 2 O 3 MOSFETs With Excellent Uniformity and >3 kV Breakdown Capability
papers.summary: This study demonstrates a wafer-scale growth of a 2-in, Si-doped $\beta $ -Ga 2 O 3 (100) epitaxial wafer and the realization of uniform, high-voltage lateral $\beta $ -Ga 2 O 3 MOSFET arrays. The 2-in homoepitaxial $\beta $ -Ga 2 O 3 (100) film grown by metal-organic chemical vapor deposition (MOCVD) exhibits excellent crystalline uniformity with an average rocking curve full width at half maximum (FWHM) of ~27.0 arcsec and a low surface roughness of less than 1 nm, alongside a uniform net doping concentration of $4.60\times 10^{{17}}$ cm -3 . The representative MOSFET delivers a threshold voltage of −31.75 V, a drain-current on / off ratio $\gt10^{{9}}$ , a specific on -resistance of 126.52 m $\Omega \cdot $ cm 2 and a breakdown voltage exceeding 3 kV. Statistical analysis across the entire wafer confirms good device uniformity, with threshold voltages ranging from −28 to −36 V, output current densities of $60\sim 75$ mA/mm, and a breakdown voltage over 3 kV. These results provide the demonstration using the 2-in $\beta $ -Ga 2 O 3 epitaxial wafer to realize high-voltage $\beta $ -Ga 2 O 3 MOSFETs with wafer-scale performance uniformity for industrial-level device application.

papers.title: Laser-transferrable GaN HEMTs based on high-quality AlN/GaN/AlN sacrificing templates
papers.summary: Laser lift-off (LLO) technology is an effective approach to fabricate transferrable GaN high-electron-mobility transistors (HEMTs) and address self-heating effects during device operation. However, conventional approaches struggle with precise control of LLO positions and structural integrity of devices, especially for those with AlN-based back barriers (BBs). Herein, we develop a laser-transferrable GaN HEMT with a μm-scale AlN BB, which is grown on a novel template including a GaN sacrificing layer (SL) and a metalorganic chemical vapor deposition-grown AlN nucleation layer (MO-AlN NL). The MO-AlN serves as the dislocation filtering layer to suppress dislocation propagation in the GaN SL, thereby creating an optimized nucleation template for the AlN BB. As such, the AlN-on-GaN epitaxy proceeds in a coherent 2D growth mode with largely reduced threading dislocations and preserved compressive strain. The devices fabricated on this AlN-BB/GaN-SL/AlN-NL tri-layer template can be integrally detached by a 266-nm UV laser, which only breaks the GaN SL and leaves an intact device active region. This work simultaneously resolves the critical challenges in μm-scale AlN-on-GaN epitaxy and laser transfer of GaN HEMTs with AlN-based BBs, offering a viable approach to laser-transferrable GaN power/RF devices with customized device structures toward improved device characteristics and thermal management.
